q: 1. Reconnaissance survey means .........
options: conducting the surveys to get the plan of the site
conducting the surveys to get contours of the site
visual inspection of the site and study of the topographical features
explain: Reconnaissance is the preliminary inspection of a site to gather information about its topography, accessibility, and general characteristics before detailed surveying begins.

q: 2. The investigation method suitable for shallow depths is .........
explain: Open excavation (trial pits) is the most direct and economical way to inspect soil strata at shallow depths, allowing for visual inspection of the soil layers.

q: 3. The minimum depth of foundation for buildings on clays is
explain: For clayey soils, foundations must be deep enough (typically 0.9m to 1.6m) to reach beyond the 'active zone' where seasonal moisture changes cause significant swelling and shrinkage.

q: 4. Soil investigation at a site are carried out to obtain the information regarding .........
options: the engineering and the physical properties of the soils
the details of the soil profile to considerable depth
the depth to ground water table and its seasonal fluctuations
explain: Comprehensive soil reports must include soil classification (properties), the sequence of layers (profile), and hydrological data (water table).

q: 5. In combined footing
options: centre of gravity of the column loads must coincide with the centre of gravity of the footing
explain: To ensure uniform soil pressure distribution under a combined footing, the geometric center (C.G.) of the footing must align with the resultant C.G. of the two column loads.

q: 6. The relationship between the ultimate bearing capacity (qu), the net ultimate bearing capacity (qnu) and the depth of footing D (r being the unit weight of the soil) is:
explain: Ultimate bearing capacity (qu) is the sum of the net ultimate bearing capacity (qnu) and the overburden pressure (γD or rD).

q: 7. The maximum load on the wooden pile should not exceed
explain: For standard timber piles, the safe design load is generally capped at 200 kN (approx. 20 tonnes) to prevent structural crushing of the wood fibers under sustained architectural loads.

q: 8. According to Rankine's theory, the minimum depth of foundation is given by .........
explain: Rankine's formula for minimum depth ensures the soil won't heave around the foundation; it uses the ratio of vertical to horizontal pressure squared.

q: 9. Osmosis is .........
options: an electrical process where fine grained cohesive soils are drained using electricity
a method to determine the depth to water table
explain: Electro-osmosis is a technique used to drain water from low-permeability soils like clay by applying a direct current between electrodes.

q: 10. Which of the following has the lowest bearing capacity?
explain: Moist or soft clay has very little internal friction and gains its strength only from cohesion, making it significantly weaker than sands or gravels.

q: 11. A pile which by itself does not carry any load but improves the bearing capacity of the soil is called .........
explain: Compaction piles are driven into loose granular soils to increase the soil's density (compactness) through vibration and displacement.

q: 12. Minimum depth of foundation on clayey soils
explain: Clayey soils are highly expansive. A minimum depth of 90 cm is required to ensure the footing rests below the 'active zone' where moisture changes cause the soil to shrink or swell.

q: 13. The distance between the flanges of the beams in any tier of a grillage foundation should be equal to .........
options: one and half times the flange width or 30 cm whichever is less
explain: To ensure proper concrete placement and compaction between the steel beams, a spacing of 1.5 to 2 times the flange width (or roughly 30cm) is maintained.

q: 14. The maximum permissible differential settlement in the case of foundations on sandy soils is generally about ..........
explain: For isolated foundations on sand, the allowable differential settlement is restricted to 25 mm to prevent structural cracking.

q: 15. The maximum permissible total settlement in the case of raft foundations clayey soils is generally about ...........
explain: Raft foundations distribute loads over a larger area; in clay, a total settlement of up to 100 mm is often considered the permissible limit.

q: 16. The thickness of staining in well foundations is generally about (where D is the diameter of the well)
explain: Staining (the wall of the well) must be thick enough to resist external earth/water pressure; D/4 is a common empirical ratio for design.

q: 17. The foundation in which a cantilever beam is provided to join two footings, is known as
explain: A strap footing uses a cantilever 'strap' beam to connect an eccentric exterior footing to an interior footing, balancing the overturning moment caused by the edge load.

q: 18. The types of foundation used to transfer heavy load is
explain: Grillage foundations consist of tiers of steel beams (I-sections) encased in concrete. They are used specifically to spread very heavy concentrated loads from columns over a large area.

q: 19. In case of foundation on black cotton soil, the most suitable method to improve the bearing capacity of soil
explain: Because black cotton soil is chemically unstable (swelling/shrinking), the most reliable method for light structures is replacing the top 1-2 meters of soil with a non-expansive material like sand or moorum.

q: 20. In rectangular foundation of which 'B' the maximum permissible eccentricity of load is limited to
explain: To ensure no tension develops at the base of a foundation (the 'middle-third' rule), the eccentricity 'e' must not exceed B/6 for rectangular bases.

q: 21. Safe bearing capacity of Black cotton soil varies from
explain: Black cotton soil is notoriously unstable due to high swelling and shrinkage; its safe bearing capacity is very low, typically 5 to 7.5 t/m².

q: 22. A group of tapering steps radiating from same point is known as ..........
explain: Winders are steps that are narrower at one end than the other, used to change the direction of the stairs.

q: 23. The building of an Engineering college should be classified as
explain: Buildings used for instructional purposes are classified as Educational buildings.

q: 24. For an ordinary double storey building, the type of foundation to be used should be
explain: Spread footings are the most common and economical choice for low-rise residential structures on stable soil.

q: 25. Raft foundations are preferred when the area required for all the individual footings is more than ........
explain: When individual footings cover more than 50% of the total building area, a raft (or mat) foundation becomes more economical and effective.

q: 26. The foundation in which a cantilever beam is provided to join two footings, is known as
explain: A strap footing uses a connecting beam (strap) to distribute loads between an eccentrically loaded footing and an interior one.

q: 27. The foundation in a building is provide to ..........
options: distribute the load over a large area
increase the overall stability of the structure
transmit the load to the bearing surface at uniform rate
explain: Foundations serve multiple purposes: load distribution, providing a level surface, and ensuring the stability of the entire building.

q: 28. When the walls are subjected to heavy loading and the bearing capacity of the soil is very low, the wall is constructed on ..........
explain: R.C.C. footings are used for heavy loads on weak soil because reinforcement allows the footing to resist tension and distribute weight more effectively.

q: 29. When heavy structural loads from columns are required to be transferred to a soil of low bearing capacity, the most economical foundation is ..........
explain: Grillage foundations (using steel beams or timber) are economical for spreading heavy column loads over a wide area without deep excavation.

q: 30. When the heavy structure is to be constructed in sandy soil, the foundation used is ..........
explain: Depending on the density and depth of the sand, piers, straps, or rafts may be used to provide adequate bearing.

q: 31. Pile foundation is generally used when the soil is ..........
explain: Piles are deep foundations used when surface soil is weak, water-logged, or unreliable, transferring loads to deeper, firmer strata.

q: 32. The type of foundation most suitable for bridges is ..........
explain: Pier foundations are commonly used for bridge structures to transfer heavy loads through water or soft soil to hard rock.

q: 33. A type of cast-in-situ pile suited for places where the ground is soft and offers little resistance to the flow of concrete, is ..........
explain: Vibro-piles use a vibrating casing that compacts the soil and ensures a dense concrete column even in soft soil conditions.

q: 34. When the pile is driven by means of water jets, water is forced through the jet pipe under a pressure of ..........
explain: Jetting uses water pressure (0.7 to 1.75 MPa) to displace soil at the pile tip, facilitating easier penetration in sandy or gravelly soils.

q: 35. In a public building, the stairs should be located near the .......... of building.
explain: In public buildings, stairs should be near the entrance for easy accessibility and fire safety evacuation.

q: 36. In pile foundation when the load is supported by friction between the pile and surrounding soil and also by resting the pile on hard stratum, such a pile is known as ..........
explain: Most piles rely on a combination of skin friction along the sides and end-bearing at the tip.

q: 37. Pile are usually not made of ..........
explain: Stainless steel is too expensive for structural foundation piles; standard steel, timber, and reinforced concrete are used instead.
